questions.q: Explain the concept of the heat budget of the Earth.

answer.text: The heat budget refers to the balance between the heat the Earth receives from the Sun and the heat it loses back to space. Since the Earth as a whole neither becomes steadily warmer nor colder over the years, the incoming and outgoing amounts of heat must be equal, maintaining a balance.

Of the solar radiation reaching the Earth, part is reflected back by clouds, dust and the surface, a quality called albedo, and part is absorbed by the atmosphere. The rest reaches the surface, which absorbs it and then re-radiates it as long-wave terrestrial radiation, eventually escaping to space.

The tropics receive more heat than they lose and so have a surplus, while the polar regions lose more than they gain and have a deficit. Winds and ocean currents transfer heat from the surplus tropics to the deficit poles.

answer: This redistribution keeps the Earth's overall temperature in balance.

questions.q: What factors cause the temperature of the air to vary from place to place?

answer.text: differs from place to place because several factors control how much heat a place receives and retains.

list: Latitude — places near the equator get more direct sun and are warmer than those near the poles
Altitude — temperature falls with height, so mountains are cooler than the plains
Distance from the sea — the sea moderates temperature, so coasts have milder climates than the interior
Ocean currents warm or cool the coasts they wash
Prevailing winds, cloud cover and the nature of the land surface further affect temperature

questions.q: How is heat distributed over the Earth, and why does it stay in balance?

answer.text: receives heat from the Sun (insolation) and loses heat back to space, and over the whole planet these balance in the heat budget.

list: The tropics receive more heat than they lose, while the polar regions lose more than they receive
If nothing moved the heat, the tropics would keep heating and the poles keep cooling
Global winds and ocean currents carry surplus heat from the tropics towards the poles
This transfer keeps the overall balance and makes much of the Earth habitable
